<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">(Figures
stated in thousands of pesos in constant currency)</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">The
transitory exceptions and regulatory guidelines established by BCRA to the application of effective IFRS, that affect the preparation
of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements are as follows:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">a)</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">According
                                            to Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6114, as amended and supplemented, and in the convergence
                                            process through IFRS, the BCRA established that since fiscal years beginning on or after
                                            January&nbsp;1, 2020, financial institutions defined as &ldquo;Group A&rdquo; by BCRA rules,
                                            in which the Bank is included, begin to apply section 5.5 &ldquo;Impairment&rdquo; of the
                                            IFRS 9 &ldquo;Financial Instruments&rdquo; (sections B5.5.1 to B5.5.55), except for the temporary
                                            exclusion for the public sector established by the Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6847.
                                            As of the date of issuance of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements, the
                                            Bank is in the process of quantifying the effect of the full application of the abovementioned
                                            standard.</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">b)</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Through
                                            Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A 7014 dated May&nbsp;14, 2020, the BCRA established for financial
                                            institutions that received debt securities of the public sector in a swap transaction, they
                                            must be initially recognized at their carrying amount as of the date of the swap transaction,
                                            without assessing if they qualify or not for derecognition under IFRS 9 standards and as
                                            a consequence, do not eventually recognize the new instruments at the market value as provided
                                            by such IFRS (see Note 9 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements).</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">If
IFRS 9 had been applied, and according an estimation calculated by the Bank, the Statement of income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30,
2024, would have recorded an increase in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo; for an amount of 2,553, in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo;
for an amount of 2,083 and in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for
an amount of 87,558, and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. In addition, it would
have been recorded in the Statement of income of the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2023 a decrease in &ldquo;Interest income&rdquo;
for an amount of 8,587,880 and on the other hand, an increase in &ldquo;Loss on net monetary position&rdquo; for an amount of 359,554
and in &ldquo;Net gain from measurement of financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss&rdquo; for an amount of 7,950,806,
and as a counterpart an increase in &ldquo;Other comprehensive income&rdquo; for that period. These changes would not have resulted into
modifications to the total shareholder equity as of those dates nor the total comprehensive income of the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30,
2024 and 2023.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><U>Applicable
Accounting Policies</U></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Except
for what was mentioned in the previous paragraphs, the accounting policies applied by the Bank comply with the IFRS as currently approved
and are applicable to the preparation of these condensed separate interim Financial Statements in accordance with the IFRS as adopted
by the BCRA through Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 7899. Generally, the BCRA does not allow the anticipated application of any IFRS,
unless otherwise expressly stated.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Note
3 to the consolidated Financial Statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2023, already issued presents further detailed descriptions of the
basis for the presentation of such Financial Statements and the main accounting policies used and the relevant information of the subsidiaries.
All that is explained therein shall apply to these condensed separate interim Financial Statements, except for the goodwill generated
by the business combination, as mentioned in Note 9, which according to BCRA Communiqu&eacute; &ldquo;A&rdquo; 6618, in the condensed
separate interim Financial Statements, is included in the net investment of the subsidiary.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><U>Going
concern</U></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">The
Bank&rsquo;s Management has made an assessment of its ability to continue as a going concern and is satisfied that it has the resources
to continue in business for the foreseeable future. Furthermore, management is not aware of any material uncertainties that may cast
significant doubt on the Bank&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern. Therefore, these condensed separate interim Financial Statements
were prepared on the going concern basis.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><U>Subsidiaries</U></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">As
mentioned in Note 1, the Bank performs certain transactions through its subsidiaries.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Subsidiaries
are all the entities controlled by the Bank. An entity controls another entity when it is exposed, or has rights, to variable returns
from its continuing involvement with such other entity and has the ability to use its power to direct the operating and financing policies
of such other entity, to affect the amounts of such returns.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">As
provided under IAS 27 &ldquo;Separate Financial Statements&rdquo;, investments in subsidiaries were accounted for using the &ldquo;equity
method&rdquo;, established in IAS 28 &ldquo;Investments in associates and joint ventures&rdquo;. When using this method, investments
are initially recognized at cost, and such amount increases or decreases to recognize investor&rsquo;s interest in profit and loss of
the entity after the date of acquisition or creation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><B>7.</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><B>LOSS
                                            ALLOWANCE FOR EXPECTED CREDIT LOSSES ON CREDIT EXPOSURES NOT MEASURED AT FAIR VALUE THROUGH
                                            PROFIT OR LOSS</B></FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">The
Bank recognizes a loss allowance for expected credit losses on all credit exposures not measured at fair value through profit or loss,
like debt instruments measured at amortized cost, debt instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments
and financial guarantee contracts (not measured at fair value through profit or loss), contract assets and lease receivables.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Note
8 discloses financial assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis and financial assets not recognized at fair value. This classification
is made pursuant to the expressed in Note 3 &ldquo;Basis for the preparation of these Financial Statements and applicable accounting
standards&rdquo;. Additionally, Note 8 explains the information related to the valuation process.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Moreover,
considering the temporary exclusion established by BCRA mentioned in Note 3 &ldquo;Applicable accounting standards&rdquo; the Bank applies
the impairment requirements for the recognition and measurement of a loss allowance for financial assets measured at amortized cost or
at fair value through other comprehensive income, except for public sector exposures. In addition, the Bank applies the impairment requirements
for guarantees granted, undrawn commitments of credit cards, checking account advance agreements and letter of credits, which are not
recognized in the condensed consolidated interim statement of financial position.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">For
the purpose of assessing the Bank&rsquo;s credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding
credit risk of financial assets and off balance items are as follows.</FONT></P>

criterion used to calculate ECL of Financial Trusts and Corporate Bonds is based on the rating granted by risk rating agencies to each
debt security type making up the financial trusts or each corporate bond series, respectively. This means that the factor to be used
will vary depending on the debt securities holdings (A or B). The EAD is assumed to be equal to the outstanding balance.</FONT></P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><B>8.</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><B>FAIR
                                            VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES</B></FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Note
10 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements describes the methods and assumptions used to determine the fair value,
both of the financial instruments recognized at fair value as of those not accounted for at such fair value in these condensed separate
interim Financial Statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">In
addition, the Bank discloses the relevant information as to instruments included in Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Even
though the Bank&rsquo;s Management has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments, any technique
to perform such estimate implies certain inherent fragility level.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White"><U>Fair value hierarchy</U></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">The
Bank uses the following hierarchy to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique
applied:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Level
                                            1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the
                                            measurement day for identical assets or liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active
                                            only if there are sufficient trading activities with respect to the volume and liquidity
                                            of the identical assets or liabilities and when there are binding and exercisable price quotes
                                            available at each period or fiscal year, as applicable.</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Level
                                            2: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the
                                            determination of the fair value recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability,
                                            either directly or indirectly. Such inputs include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities
                                            in active markets, quoted prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable
                                            inputs other than quoted prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities,
                                            and credit spreads. In addition, adjustments to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition
                                            or location of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable to
                                            the valued instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that
                                            are significant to the entire measurement, the Bank will classify the instruments as Level
                                            3.</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">-</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="background-color: White">Level
                                            3: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the
                                            determination of the fair value recognized or disclosed are not based on observable market
                                            information.</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Note 10 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements, details the valuation techniques and significant unobservable inputs used in
the valuation of assets at Level 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><U>Changes
in fair value levels</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank monitors the availability
of information in the market to evaluate the classification of financial instruments into the fair value hierarchy as well as the resulting
determination of transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3 at each period end.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Except for the foregoing, as of September&nbsp;30,
2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023, the Bank has not recognized any transfers between levels 1, 2 and 3.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.5in">9.2</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Banco BMA SAU (formerly known as Banco
                                            Ita&uacute; Argentina SA)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On August&nbsp;23, 2023, Banco Macro
SA entered into a stock purchase agreement with Ita&uacute; Unibanco Holding SA, through its affiliates Ita&uacute; Unibanco SA, Banco
Ita&uacute; BBA SA and Ita&uacute; Consultoria de Valores Mobili&aacute;rios e Participa&ccedil;&otilde;es SA (collectively, &ldquo;Ita&uacute;&rdquo;),
pursuant to which, subject to certain conditions (substantially the approval of the transaction by the BCRA), the Bank would acquire
from Ita&uacute; the shares representing 100% of the capital stock and votes of Banco Ita&uacute; Argentina SA,&nbsp;Ita&uacute; Asset
Management SA and Ita&uacute; Valores SA.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.75in; text-align: justify">On November&nbsp;2, 2023, the Board
of Directors of the BCRA authorized the abovementioned purchase. Detailed information on this transaction is included in Note 11.2 to
the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Key management personnel are those
persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Bank, directly or indirectly.
The Bank considers as key management personnel, for the purposes of IAS 24, the members of the Board of Directors and the senior management
members of the Risk Management Committee, the Assets and Liabilities Committee and the Senior Credit Committee.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Fiscal years 2019 and 2020</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">As decided by the Board of Directors
in the meeting held on May&nbsp;11, 2020, considering certain case law on the matter assessed by its legal counsel and tax advisors,
on May&nbsp;26 the Bank filed with the Administraci&oacute;n Federal de Ingresos P&uacute;blicos (AFIP, for its acronym in Spanish),
current Agencia de Recaudaci&oacute;n y Control Aduanero (ARCA, for its acronym in Spanish), as established by Decree No.&nbsp;953/2024
of the National Executive Branch, its annual income tax return considering the total effect of the inflation adjustment on income tax
(see section a) iv) of Note 21 to the condensed consolidated interim Financial Statements). As a result, the current income tax determined
by the Bank for fiscal year 2019 amounted to 7,002,124 (not restated). The same criterion was applied to determine the annual income
tax report for 2020, which generated accrued income tax for the Bank for such fiscal year that amounted to 9,933,210 (not restated).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">In addition, on July&nbsp;23, 2021,
the Bank filed a reimbursement action with the former AFIP requesting the refund of 254,305 (not restated) paid as income tax for the
2020 tax period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding to the tax periods mentioned
in previous paragraphs, on November&nbsp;1, 2021, the former AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit. Regarding to the 2019
tax period, on June&nbsp;15, 2023, the former AFIP notified the closure of the audit, with a tax adjustment. The adjustment was rejected
by the Bank, alleging that said adjustment is under discussion in a judicial case through a declaratory action for certainty.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Along with the filings mentioned in
the first paragraph of this section, on December&nbsp;28, 2021, the Bank filed petitions for declaratory judgment with the Federal Administrative
Contentious Court for the periods under analysis. The file 22274/2021, for the fiscal year 2019, is in process in Court No.&nbsp;12 and
the file 22278/2021, for the fiscal year 2020, is in process in Court No.&nbsp;1.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in"><U>Fiscal year 2021</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On October&nbsp;17, 2022, Banco Macro
SA filed a reimbursement action with the former AFIP requesting the refund of 382,189 (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2021
tax period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding to the tax period abovementioned,
on January&nbsp;3, 2023, the former AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit. On April&nbsp;8, 2024 the former AFIP notified
the closure of the audit, without tax adjustment.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Fiscal year 2022</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On June&nbsp;30, 2023, Banco Macro
SA filed a reimbursement action with the former AFIP requesting the refund of 654,673 paid as income tax for the 2022 tax period.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding to the tax period abovementioned,
on 16 November, 2023, the former AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit. On August&nbsp;6, 2024 the former AFIP notified
the closure of the audit, without tax adjustment.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify"><U>Reimbursement actions &ndash; Fiscal
years 2013 to 2017 and 2018</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On October&nbsp;24, 2019, Banco Macro
SA filed with the former AFIP two reimbursement actions under the terms established by the first paragraph of section 81, Law No.&nbsp;11683
requesting the reimbursement of 4,782,766 and 5,015,451 (not restated amounts) paid to tax authorities as income tax during 2013 through
2017 and 2018 tax periods, respectively, arising from the impossibility to apply the adjustment for inflation and other adjustment mechanisms
set forth by income tax Law (prior to the amendments introduced by Laws No.&nbsp;27430 and 27468 for 2013 through 2017 tax periods, and
as revised in 2019 and amended for the 2018 tax period), plus the related compensatory interest (SIGEA [case and file management system]
files No.&nbsp;19144-14224/2019 and 19144-14222/2019). Since tax authorities have not yet issued a resolution with respect to the abovementioned
claims, on August&nbsp;7, 2020, the Bank filed both reimbursement requests under the terms of the second paragraph of the abovementioned
section 81, Law No.&nbsp;11683 with the Federal Contentious and Administrative Trial Courts, which are pending in Courts No.&nbsp;8 and
2 of such jurisdiction, respectively (cases No.&nbsp;11285/2020 and 11296/2020). Currently, in connection with the file for the 2018
tax period, the evidence stage is closed and the process for allegation was delivered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding to the tax periods mentioned
in the previous paragraph, on December&nbsp;19, 2019, the former AFIP notified the beginning of the income tax audit for the 2018 tax
period, and on May&nbsp;3, 2021, it notified the beginning of the income tax audit for periods 2013 to 2017, both inclusive. On October&nbsp;4,
2021, the former AFIP ended the audit for periods 2013 through 2017 as the Bank had exercised in due time its right to resort to justice,
and that the admission of reimbursement is subject to a court decision.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED SEPARATE INTERIM FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><B>AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2024</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Translation of Financial Statements originally
issued in Spanish &ndash; See Note 41)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">(Figures stated in thousands of pesos in constant
currency)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">Regarding to the periods 2013 to 2017,
on October&nbsp;8, 2024, the Federal Contentious and Administrative Trial Court No.&nbsp;8 issued a favorable sentence to the Bank's
request, in which it admitted the recovery action for the amount of $4,782,766 plus compensatory interest. The aforementioned court considered
that the lack of application of the tax inflation adjustment generated the taxation of a confiscatory income tax in the periods 2013/2017.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">On October&nbsp;16, 2024, the former
AFIP appealed the sentence.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><B>26.</B></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><B>ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURES IN THE STATEMENT
                                            OF CASH FLOWS</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Statement of cash flows presents
the changes in cash and cash equivalents derived from operating activities, investing activities and financing activities during the
period. For the preparation of the statement of cash flows the Bank adopted the indirect method for Operating Activities and the direct
method for Investment Activities and Financing Activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The Bank considers as &ldquo;Cash
and cash equivalents&rdquo; the item Cash and deposits in banks and those financial assets that are readily convertible to known amounts
of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">For the preparation of the Statement
of cash flows the Bank considered the following:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Operating activities: the normal revenue-producing
                                            activities of the Bank as well as other activities that cannot qualify as investing or financing
                                            activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Investing activities: the acquisition,
                                            sale and disposal by other means of long-term assets and other investments not included in
                                            cash and cash equivalents.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 18pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 10.35pt">-</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Financing activities: activities that result
                                            in changes in the size and composition of the shareholders&acute; equity and liabilities
                                            of the Bank and that are not part of the operating or investing activities.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.25in; text-align: justify">The table below presents the reconciliation
